text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO breach detected for streaming tail latency (p95/p99) in eu-west-2. Multiple svc routes showing increased TLS handshake times and stalls. Auto-mitigation rules did not fully resolve. Paging on-call now.

claire: I'm on it — oncall. Jumping into traces and tcpdump. Any recent network changes?

ben: Not aware of infra config changes in last 24h. Quick check: no rolling upgrades. I'll pull route tables and NAT gateway metrics.

alice: Observability shows p95 for streaming connections jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms starting ~18:12 UTC. p99 is ~2.3s.

claire: Reproducing logs: TLS handshake durations spiking, a lot of SYN->SYN/ACK retransmits. Could be cross-zone path noise.

ellie: Customer reports: intermittent stalls for long-lived streams, manifests as client re-buffering. Affects ~8% of requests in eu-west-2 in last 20m.

dave: tagging @ben @claire - please confirm if NAT ephemeral pool exhaustion or conntrack pressure. If so we should scale NAT or adjust ephemeral port reuse.

ben: Checking NAT metrics...

infra-bot: NAT24-A (eu-west-2a) ephemeral_port_usage=89%, conntrack_entries=78%, queue_depth=5
infra-bot: NAT42-B (eu-west-2b) ephemeral_port_usage=91%, conntrack_entries=85%, queue_depth=12

ben: NAT B is high. But handshake timeouts look like SYN retransmits across AZ boundaries. I'm running a fast tcpdump on proxy->backend path.

claire: Also seeing DNS resolution jitter for a small subset of hostnames; not system-wide but enough to cause re-resolves and additional handshakes.

ellie: Any camera logs for LB health checks? Might be transient backend slow-paths.

alice: From traces: majority of delayed tokens correlate with initial TLS handshake RTTs, not application processing.

claire: Running command:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.32.45.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
```
Will upload snippet.

ben: Route tables are fine. No recent route changes. I see increased packet retransmit counters on vpc-peering-2 between AZ A and AZ B.

ben: quick dig on resolver used by services:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +time=2 @10.20.30.5 api.service.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
;; Query time: 320 msec
```
Query time 320ms for a local resolver is anomalous.

claire: Ok, two hypotheses: (1) inter-AZ fabric transient packet loss causing TLS handshake retries and retransmits, (2) NAT ephemeral saturation amplifying retries and forcing fallbacks.

dave: Mitigation options: 1) Temporarily force streaming traffic to single-AZ pools to avoid cross-AZ hops (can increase capacity pressure but reduces inter-AZ handshake pain). 2) Increase NAT capacity / rotate to spare NATs. 3) Apply route flaps mitigation (increase MTU/fragment retries) — risky.

ellie: For customer impact, start a status note: small fraction of streaming sessions degrade, some customers report rebuffering. No data exfil or auth failures.

sam: Drafting status page update now. Will note degraded streaming performance in eu-west-2, working on mitigation.

ben: I can spin up an extra NAT pair in eu-west-2b and shift some routes. Doing now:
```
# scale NAT autoscale group
aws ec2 run-instances --launch-template nat-template --count 2 --region eu-west-2
```
ETA ~5m.

infra-bot: New NAT instances launching. health=starting

claire: While NAT comes up, let's try sticky-AZ routing for streaming ingress. Ellie, can you update the envoy/router config to prefer same-AZ backends for long-lived streams?

ellie: On it. Pushing a temporary route preference change to staging then can roll to prod for eu-west-2.

alice: FYI I see increased TLS handshake failures denoted by client-side renegotiations and aborted sessions in logs: sample:
```
[2026-03-15T18:25:12Z] connid=12 handshake_ms=1789 retries=3 cause=timed_out
```
That aligns with p99 spike.

dave: If we can route streaming traffic AZ-local, we may mitigate the path noise quickly. Ben, once NAT is up, can we drain some cross-AZ NAT routes?

ben: NATs up. Switching a subset of outbound routes to NAT24-A and NAT42-B local affinity. Will redistribute flow tables.

infra-bot: Route update applied to streaming-route-table-3: prefer-local-az=true for tag=streaming session_affinity=az

claire: After routing change we see handshake latency dropping in tail buckets. p95 dropped to ~240ms within 90s. p99 still elevated but improving.

ellie: Rolling change notes: applied AZ affinity, spun up additional NATs, no config rollbacks required.

alice: Continued traces show residual DNS queries still slow for ~1% of requests; investigating resolver health. Might be a separate issue but low volume.

ben: I'm continuing to monitor vpc peering counters. Retransmits down ~60% after routing change.

dave: Good. Next steps: keep NAT capacity elevated for 2h, monitor p95/p99, and run a full DNS healthcheck sweep. If DNS issues persist, failover to alternate resolver cluster.

ops-manager: Can someone create a short incident summary for postmortem? Include timeline, mitigations, impact, customers affected, and follow-ups. Assign action owners.

claire: I'll take incident lead and write initial summary. Assigning follow-ups:
- ben: root-cause deep dive on VPC peering packet loss (due EoR?).
- alice: collect handshake traces and assemble flame graphs for TLS path.
- ellie: evaluate sticky-AZ affinity as a longer-term mitigation and potential perf tradeoffs.
- sam: update customer comms and coordinate with support for impacted accounts.

sam: Status page updated: "Degraded streaming performance in eu-west-2. Mitigation in progress; restored for majority of traffic. Investigating residual DNS latency."

infra-bot: Alert auto-resolve: SLO breach cleared for majority of streams; continued monitoring enabled.

claire: Handoff to next on-call in 30m. I'll finish the incident doc and escalate to networking team if VPC peering counters remain high after 4h.

dave: Thanks all. If you see any customer escalation ping me directly. :thumbsup:

ops-manager: Marking incident as "mitigated - monitoring". Document link TBD.

claire: Final notes: root cause likely transient inter-AZ fabric packet loss amplified by high NAT ephemeral utilization and slow local DNS responses. Immediate mitigation: AZ-affinity routing + extra NAT capacity. Long-term actions: network infra healthcheck, DNS resolver redundancy, and runbook update for streaming AZ-failover.

ellie: handing off to @dave for night watch.

dave: taking handoff. Will run checks every 15m for the next 2h.

sam: logfile snippets and pcap dropped into /incidents/3298765432/artifacts/ for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Metrics will auto-collect for postmortem.

claire: thanks everyone.
